about.expert_notes: Permutation (randomisation) test on a scale-free statistic: holdout skill 1 - L(model) / L(null forecast) on each dataset (the null forecast is the last training value of an integrated series, else its mean). Null: models with drivers keep the result and get their drivers block-permuted jointly (so trend, season and controls cannot pass on their own; a model that ignores its drivers is tested as one without); models without drivers get the d-th differences of the result permuted i.i.d. and re-integrated from the original start (d from the ARIMA order or ADF/KPSS), which keeps the integration order and the increments' distribution but destroys predictable dynamics. Without a time order the result is permuted across rows and the statistic is the holdout error. p = (1 + #{perm >= real}) / (K + 1).

assumptions: The count of an area is Poisson around its expected count times its relative risk
Neighbouring areas have similar risks (kind icar, car or bym2), or the areas are independent (kind iid)
An island is linked to the area with the closest border, unless you change the islands setting
The covariate has the same effect in every area
avoid_when: You have the location of each case, not counts for each area (use a point model)
The values are not counts, for example a mean income for each area
You must predict areas that are not on the map (the graph has only the fitted areas)
The data change over time and you want a forecast
data_needs: A count of cases and an expected count (age-standardised) for each area
One covariate for each area, for example a percentage
Which areas are neighbours (an adjacency matrix), for example from shared borders
The outline of each area (polygon points), for the maps and to link islands
about.example: Map lip cancer in the 56 districts of Scotland from 1975 to 1980. Get the smoothed relative risk of each district, find the 19 districts where the risk is surely above the national level, and see the effect of outdoor work fall from 1.96 to 1.5 per 10 points when neighbours share their risk.
about.expert_notes: Poisson(E_i exp(b0 + b1 x_i + u_i)) with x = (covariate - mean) / covariate_scale (pymc-challenges E18). kind: poisson (u = 0), iid (u = sigma theta), icar (sigma pm.ICAR(W), soft sum-to-zero), car (pm.CAR with alpha ~ U(0, 1), tau = 1 / sigma^2; alpha piles up near 1 and b0 mixes slowly) or bym2 (Riebler et al. 2016: u = sigma (sqrt(rho / s) phi + sqrt(1 - rho) theta), s = geometric mean of diag(pinv(D - W)), rho ~ Beta(1, 1)). b0, b1 ~ N(0, 1), sigma ~ HalfNormal(1). islands: link_nearest joins each area without neighbours (then each separate piece) to the area with the closest polygon vertex; isolate keeps them (iid and icar only: an isolated ICAR node has a flat prior); error refuses. The pointwise log-likelihood is always kept, so elpd_loo compares the kinds (Pareto k is often high: one parameter per area). A mask_block split over area holds districts out of the likelihood but keeps them in the graph (leave-areas-out). simulate draws new area effects per draw with a hand-written ICAR sampler (eigenvectors of the Laplacian), as pm.ICAR cannot be forward-sampled. On the Scottish data the AFF effect drops from 0.67 (iid) to about 0.4 (spatial kinds): spatial confounding.
outputs: The smoothed relative risk of each area, with a range
The probability that the relative risk of each area is above 1
The expected cases of each area, and new counts and maps (simulate)
The effect of the covariate, the size of the area effects and the share of them that follows the map (rho, kind bym2)

assumptions: The hour of the day and the day of the year change the direction smoothly (a few harmonics of each)
Rows are independent when the hour and the season are known
Activity: the density over the day is smooth, and an animal is fully active at the peak of its curve
avoid_when: The values are not on a circle (for example a temperature)
You need the speed of the wind as well as its direction (the model uses only the direction)
The wind is calm (a calm has no direction: remove those rows first)
You need forecasts of the next hours from the last values (the model uses only the hour and the day of the year)
data_needs: One row for each report or record, with the angle in degrees, radians or hours
For directions: the hour of the day (0 to 24) and the day of the year of each row
For activity: the group (species) of each record
about.example: Hourly winds at Santa Barbara airport come from the west-southwest in the afternoon (the sea breeze) and from the east at night. The ocelot and the agouti share only 30% of their daily activity.
about.expert_notes: pymc-challenges E81. Von Mises regression with the canonical link: natural parameters eta = F B, log p = eta . (cos t, sin t) - log(2 pi I0(|eta|)), concave in B (no wrapped prior, no seam at +-pi, no second mode of the tan-half link). F holds an intercept and harmonics of the hour and the day of year plus their products (19 features by default). Kinds: von_mises, projected_normal (angle of N(F B, I)), regime_mixture (two von Mises regimes on fewer features, the second one's probability through a logistic gate on all features, labels anchored by the prior directions), activity (log-Fourier density per group, a_k, b_k ~ N(0, (tau/k)^2), fitted through the trigonometric moments, tau ~ HalfNormal(2)). Priors N(0, 2) on intercepts and N(0, 1) on the other coefficients; regime_mixture instead centres each regime intercept on 2 (cos mu_r, sin mu_r) with sd 1, gives the gate intercept N(0, 1.5) and the other coefficients N(0, 1). Pointwise log densities (per radian) support elpd_loo across kinds. Activity level 1 / (2 pi max f) (Rowcliffe et al. 2014), overlap Delta = int min(f_i, f_j).
outputs: The mean direction and the mean resultant length for each row and for each block of hours or each group
The density of the angles around the circle for each block or group, with a range
Simulated angles for new hours and days
Activity: the fraction of the day each group is active, and the overlap of each pair of groups

assumptions: The sky is a Gaussian random field with the same statistics in all directions
The power in each bin is the reference power times a free factor
The noise is Gaussian and independent from pixel to pixel
The patch is flat. The model adds a border without data so that the edges need not repeat
avoid_when: The patch is large (more than about 20 degrees): the flat-sky approximation fails
The map has strong foreground residuals outside the mask
You need polarisation or lensing (the model has temperature only)
data_needs: A temperature map on a regular grid of pixels in uK, with NaN where the mask removes a pixel
The noise sd of each pixel
A reference spectrum D_ell (for example the Planck best fit) for multipoles 0, 1, 2, ... and optionally the pixel window of the source map
The pixel size and the beam width of the map
about.example: The Planck SMICA map around the Large Magellanic Cloud (16 % of the pixels masked) gives a pixel sd of 2.5 uK where there are data and about 90 uK in the hole. Its amplitude is within 2 % of the Planck spectrum.
about.expert_notes: Field-level inference on a flat periodic torus (the raster plus an unobserved border). The Hartley coefficients of the sky are independent Gaussians with the reference spectrum folded through the beam, the pixel windows and aliasing, times exp(q_b) per bandpower bin (flat prior on q_b). A Wandelt-Eriksen Gibbs sampler alternates a constrained realisation by preconditioned conjugate gradients (dense preconditioner on the large scales), an inverse-gamma draw of each bandpower and a non-centred rescaling move (Metropolis). NumPy and FFTs only, no NUTS. The amplitude and tilt come from the exact Gaussian posterior of a linear model of the binned q_b. No pointwise LOO: all pixels share one latent field.
outputs: Probable sky maps (constrained realisations) with a mean and an sd for each pixel
The bandpowers (D_ell in uK^2) and their ratio to the reference
The amplitude and the tilt of the spectrum relative to the reference
Simulated maps of other patches with the same spectrum

assumptions: Each word has a region in colour space with a smooth shape
The speakers share the shapes. Each speaker can use a word more or less and move its boundaries (setting kind: hierarchical)
Given the speaker, each chip is named independently of the other chips
A missing answer does not depend on the chip or the word

The words are not colour names, or the items do not have a colour
You want to know which chip is the best example of a word (the model gives the chip that the most speakers agree on, which is a different thing)

about.expert_notes: Multinomial logistic regression on 10 standardised quadratic CIELAB features (1, L, a, b, L^2, a^2, b^2, ab, La, Lb), the well-conditioned natural form of Gaussian categories (pymc-challenges E77). W ~ ZeroSumNormal(3) over terms. kind: hierarchical adds speaker effects on the intercept and the linear weights, W_s = W + sd z_s with sd ~ HalfNormal(1) and z ~ ZeroSumNormal(1) (non-centred). The likelihood is a potential over the observed responses (pooled: the chip x term count table). features: grid_line / grid_circle are the printed-grid variants (hue as a line or a circle) for an elpd_loo ladder. New speakers get fresh effects per draw (new-level strategy hyperprior); the language-level shares average 20 simulated speakers per draw. Pointwise log-likelihood is per chip (leave-one-chip-out). Effective categories = exp(I(chip; term)).

assumptions: Cells move at random and divide until the columns are full
No cells go in or out at the two edges of the image
All columns have the same maximum number of cells
With the delay setting, the cells start slowly after the scratch
avoid_when: The columns do not have equal width
You have positions of single cells, not counts (count them in columns first)
The cells move in a direction, for example to a chemical signal (the model has only random movement)
You need a forecast further ahead than the model permits without a new fit
data_needs: A count of cells for each column and each time, with the time in whole hours
Columns of equal width, with the position of the center of each column in um
Counts at the first time for all columns (the model starts from them)
about.example: Count PC-3 cells in 38 columns of 50 um at 0, 12, 24, 36 and 48 hours. Get the speed of the cell front (about 27 um per hour) and forecast the counts at 60 hours.
about.expert_notes: Fisher-KPP reaction-diffusion u_t = a(t) (D u_xx + lam u (1 - u)), a(t) = tanh(beta t) with the delay setting, else 1 (pymc-challenges E50). Method of lines: finite-volume Laplacian with zero-flux boundaries, explicit Euler steps of 1/steps_per_hour hours in pytensor.scan. The PDE starts from the counts at the first fitted time (conditioned on, not in the likelihood, kept in the bundle). Counts are Poisson with mean K u. Priors: D ~ LogNormal(log 1000, 1) um^2/h, lam ~ LogNormal(log 0.05, 1) 1/h, K ~ Normal(122, 15), beta ~ LogNormal(log 0.1, 1) 1/h. The fit refuses settings where D dt / dx^2 > 1/2 at the 99% prior quantile of D (CFL bound). wave_speed = 2 sqrt(D lam). Without the delay, D is biased low by a factor of about four on the PC-3 data, and LOO prefers the delay model.

assumptions: The variables have a joint normal distribution after the fit centres and scales them
A link is present when the partial correlation is larger than the threshold (0.1 by default)
With kind neighbourhood: most variables have only a few direct links
avoid_when: You need the direction of each link (cause and effect): the network has no arrows
The samples come from different conditions or treatments (fit each one separately)
The relations are strongly curved or the values have very long tails (the model sees only straight-line relations)
You have more than about 50 variables (the fit becomes slow)
data_needs: One value for each variable in each sample, with no missing values
Samples that are independent and come from one condition
Optional: a known network as a matrix of 0 and 1, to compare with
about.example: Measure 11 proteins in 853 T cells. Get 8 links with a probability above 0.5, for example Erk with Akt and Raf with Mek. Compare them with the 20 links of the published signalling network: 7 of the 8 are in it.
about.expert_notes: Gaussian graphical model (pymc-challenges E19). kind dense: z ~ MvNormal(mu, L L^T) on the standardised data, L ~ LKJCholeskyCov(eta = 2, sd ~ Exponential(1)), mu ~ Normal(0, 1); the precision Omega = L^-T L^-1 comes from a triangular solve and the partial correlations rho_jk = -Omega_jk / sqrt(Omega_jj Omega_kk) are deterministics. An edge is |rho| > delta (default 0.1), so P(edge) = P(|rho| > delta | data). The LKJ prior is a dense-graph prior (83% prior probability for each edge in 11 dimensions). kind neighbourhood: Meinshausen-Buhlmann neighbourhood selection, one regularised horseshoe regression per variable in one model (tau0 = p0 / (P - 1 - p0) / sqrt(n), c^2 ~ InvGamma(2, 2)), with AND, OR or symmetric rho = sign(B_jk) sqrt(B_jk B_kj) rules; it conditions on the other variables, so it scores only the graph. A horseshoe directly on Omega is not offered: most of its prior is not positive definite. use_when: Values cover several orders of magnitude

assumptions: The step moves exact values of 0 and 1 a small distance inwards
avoid_when: Values are not between 0 and 1

use_when: You model a rate or a share

assumptions: The step learns the largest value from the training data only
avoid_when: Your data has extreme outliers (they set the scale)

outputs: The same columns between -1 and 1

about.title: Scale to between -1 and 1
use_when: A model needs values in a fixed range

assumptions: The step learns the average from the training data only and uses it again for new data
avoid_when: The model scales the data itself

use_when: Markets or channels are very different in size

assumptions: Use this step before you fill the gaps
avoid_when: There are no gaps
data_needs: Columns that can have gaps

outputs: One 0/1 column for each input column

about.title: Flag missing values
use_when: The fact that a value is missing gives you information

assumptions: The categories in the training data are the important categories. New categories follow a rule
avoid_when: A category has hundreds of values (give them numbers instead)

about.title: Categories to yes/no columns
use_when: A model needs numbers but you have categories

assumptions: The codes are never real values
avoid_when: All numbers are real measurements
data_needs: Columns with placeholder codes

outputs: The same columns with gaps in place of the codes
about.summary_plain: Marks placeholder numbers, such as -99 or 9999, as missing. Some systems use these numbers for 'unknown'.

use_when: Your source uses codes such as -99 for missing values

use_when: Your data is daily, but you plan and report by week or month
A model needs weekly data

assumptions: Missing values or a mask mark the padding cells

use_when: A model works on individual observations, such as shopping trips

assumptions: The gaps have a mark, so the model can ignore them
avoid_when: Your data is already a grid
data_needs: A group column and an order in each group
about.example: Households with 3 trips and 1 trip become a 2 by 3 grid with two empty cells.
outputs: A grid of groups by position, and a mask of the real cells

about.title: Put groups side by side
use_when: A model needs a grid of groups by position, such as households by trip

assumptions: The drift continues at the same rate into the future
